name: date-no-step
row: crossing midnight steps the date by exactly one

name: wrap-to-middle
row: Jun 20 at 23:59, stepped past midnight, becomes Mar 20
old: SKY.mjd = SKY.mjd + 1 > sd[1] || SKY.mjd < sd[0] ? sd[0] : SKY.mjd + 1;
new: SKY.mjd = SKY.mjd + 1 > sd[1] || SKY.mjd < sd[0] ? sd[2] : SKY.mjd + 1; /* @negtest */

name: est-all-year
row: utcOffset follows the US rule (and the first-visit row: EDT)

name: no-fall-back
row: the clock changes at 02:00 as Raleigh's does
old: if (SKY.mjd === off && SKY.dst) { t -= 1; SKY.dst = false; }
new: if (false && SKY.mjd === off && SKY.dst) { t -= 1; SKY.dst = false; } /* @negtest */

name: date-not-saved
row: the date is saved at midnight and a second visit comes back to it

name: jd-ignores-dst
row: the sun from the date (the sun at 9 am and 5 pm), May 5 sunrise and sunset, one sun vs astronomy-engine

name: lat-90
row: one sun (the observer and the sun vs astronomy-engine); the pole of date; Polaris
old: const OBS_SKY = { latDeg: OBS.lat, lonEastDeg: OBS.lon, heightM: 0 };
new: const OBS_SKY = { latDeg: 90, lonEastDeg: OBS.lon, heightM: 0 }; /* @negtest */

name: lon-sign
row: one sun; the sun from the date; LST
old: const OBS_SKY = { latDeg: OBS.lat, lonEastDeg: OBS.lon, heightM: 0 };
new: const OBS_SKY = { latDeg: OBS.lat, lonEastDeg: -OBS.lon, heightM: 0 }; /* @negtest */

name: star-no-transpose
row: the planets are drawn where they are (Jupiter's pixel)

name: mw-no-transpose
row: the Milky Way all round the sky (the one-crossing row misses it: the wrong frame puts that patch at b = -6, still on the band)

name: stars-of-date
row: the 22:00 sky (eight stars within 0.05 deg); the pole of date

name: moon-placeholder
row: the moon in its real place
new: SKY.moon = (() => { const h = (SKY.hour + 12.8 - SKY.solarNoon) / 24 * TAU, la = OBS.lat * RAD, d = -SKY.decl * 0.6 * RAD; return [-Math.cos(d) * Math.sin(h), Math.sin(la) * Math.sin(d) + Math.cos(la) * Math.cos(d) * Math.cos(h), Math.sin(d) * Math.cos(la) - Math.cos(d) * Math.sin(la) * Math.cos(h)]; })(); /* @negtest */

name: planets-as-j2000
row: the planets are drawn where they are (vertices and Jupiter's pixel)

name: planets-frozen
row: the planets are drawn where they are (the vertices)

name: planets-frozen-gpu
row: the planets' vertices on the GPU follow the date (a pixel cannot see it: Jupiter moves under a pixel between 13:00 and 22:00)

name: no-star-pass
row: one POINTS draw per pass; Jupiter's pixel; star pixels at midnight

name: stars-by-day
row: one POINTS draw per pass (none by day): the draw gate alone (the gain still carries the night)

name: stars-not-faded
row: no star pixels at noon; one POINTS draw per pass (none by day)

name: stars-twilight
row: the stars fade with the night (Polaris at SKY.night 0.5)

name: hash-star-left
row: with STARS.on false at midnight no isolated bright pixels

name: no-ridge-test
row: a star behind the distant hills is hidden (Capella at 00:30 on May 6)

name: mw-world-coords
row: the Milky Way where the suite's own galactic plane says it is

name: mw-by-day

new: if (uMwGain > 0.0 && d.y >= ridge) c += uMwGain * zmhMilkyWay(transpose(uStarM) * d) * MILKY_WAY_RGB * smoothstep(0.0, 0.1, d.y);${"" /* @negtest */}

name: no-world-flip-sun
row: the sun is drawn where it is (also the one-crossing Milky Way row, through the mirrored moon glow)
